items.rationale: Theft damage to the frame is covered at the pre-loss specification under §§2.3.1 and 7.1.9. The €500 mobility limit is shared rateably across an estimated €998 of covered repair and recovery costs, giving €229 × 500/998.
The brakes were damaged in the theft and equivalent replacements are covered under §§2.3.1 and 7.1.7(b). The rateable share under §4.2.2 is €140 × 500/998.
The tracker helped locate the bike, but no theft damage to the tracker itself is established. Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude its replacement; €35 is a conditional gross estimate only.
This is routine servicing of an unaffected bicycle, excluded by §§3.1.6 and 7.1.5. The conditional estimate for one service is €125 gross.
Neither purchase replaces an accessory shown to have been taken or damaged, so §§3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude both. The conditional gross estimate for the two pieces together is €150.
Section 7.1.7(f) covers freight attributable to the damaged bicycle or its repair parts, not freight for unrelated purchases. On the repair attribution, the rateable amount is €26 × 500/998.

Sections 7.1.8(f) and 7.1.10 require a necessary attendance tied to covered work, which this generic vehicle charge does not establish. If substantiated, adding €77 to the covered pool would give €77 × 500/1,075.
Fitting the replacement frame and brakes is covered by §7.1.7(c), provided it is not the same work charged again as hourly labour under §7.1.8(g). The rateable estimate is €113 × 500/998.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers sundries consumed in the insured repair, but this generic line does not establish that link on a mixed invoice as required by §7.1.10. If €15 of repair sundries were substantiated, the share would be €15 × 500/1,013.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers apprentice labour if it served the theft repair and is not already included in assembly. On that basis, one hour gives €55 × 500/998.
Sections 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.10 cover this hour to the extent it is distinct labour for the theft repair rather than the second bicycle's service. One hour at the €54 full rate gives €54 × 500/998.
The locksmith's first attendance was necessary to release the recovered bicycle and is covered in its own right under §5.2.2(a). One estimated €45 call-out gives €45 × 500/998.
Section 5.2.2(b) expressly covers cutting and removing the lock to release the bicycle. The two invoiced pieces give 2 × €54 × 500/998.

A further attendance is covered under §§5.2.2(a) and 7.1.8(f) only if the recovery actually required it; no need for a return after release is shown. If justified, a €45 charge would give €45 × 500/1,043.
The yard required payment before releasing the bicycle, so §5.2.2(c) covers the unavoidable fee. The €100 charge plus 19% VAT is €119 gross, reduced rateably to €119 × 500/998 under §4.2.2.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) exclude claim processing, which is distinct from the yard's mandatory release fee. The conditional gross estimate for one processing fee is €15.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers every labour grade employed on releasing the lock, subject to the duplicate-cost rule in §7.1.8(g). One separately chargeable hour gives €55 × 500/998.
Skilled labour for releasing the bicycle is covered by §5.2.2(b) if it is not already billed in the cutting charge. One hour at the €54 full rate gives €54 × 500/998.
